title: Live timeline tap starts Apple Music twice on iPhone Safari
acceptance: One still-finger tap on a Live timeline track produces exactly one Apple Music prepare on iPhone Safari (?playback-timing=1 shows one #N prepare and no #N cancelled about 60-115 ms later).
A runtime or LiveTimeline test reproduces a pointer down then up with a small movement and fails before the fix.
Next, Previous, auto-advance and a drag that rests past the throttle window keep their current behaviour.
nextAction: Find why the release commits a second seek after the pointer-down preview on iPhone: likely a few pixels of finger movement makes seekRelease's firedLast check miss, so the release is a new discrete seek (apps/web/src/components/LiveTimeline.tsx, LiveMode.tsx seekRelease). Fix, then re-run the tap step on iPhone. Agent-created: Backlog until the owner sets Ready.

evidence.summary: Owner's iPhone Safari run on production af800c8 (Worker d05bb48f, SPA assets/index-ChxMwIpX.js), 2026-11-03 about 13:28-13:58 MST, ?playback-timing=1, class [QA] Audit Experienced Cycle (24 Apple Music tracks); console read by the Air conductor through Safari Web Inspector, plus the owner's screen recordings. Three of three still-finger timeline taps fired two starts: #3 cancelled +115 ms then #4; #6 cancelled +61 ms then #7; #41 cancelled +62 ms then #42. The bounded wait settled each (next-start-released ... settled), so no banner showed, but each tap paid an extra setQueue. Next (#46-#48) fired one start each.
Timeline previews on pointer down and commits on release; #669 made release skip the provider call only when the throttle already sent exactly this gesture's position.
